# Symmetry derivation workshop

Entry `#compute/symmetry-workshop`; classroom `#classroom/crystal?module=workshop`. The workshop turns symmetry constraints into a termwise explained experiment using original NumPy-only core `symmetry_workshop.py`.

## Explicit model space

Consider a Hermitian 2×2 Hamiltonian near two-dimensional Γ for a real-spin doublet with common parity:

H(k)=d₀(k)I+d_x(k)σ_x+d_y(k)σ_y+d_z(k)σ_z。

Each d component expands in real-coefficient monomials {1,k_x,k_y,k_x²,k_xk_y,k_y²}, giving 24 unconstrained real coefficients. k is a reduced teaching coordinate and plotted energies use eV. Coefficients are not material fits; no lattice constant converts k to Å⁻¹.

Candidates: common curvature, Rashba linear, specified-axis Dresselhaus, constant σ_z/σ_x. Constraints solve full24D space, not merely candidates.

“Dresselhaus-like” refers to the explicitly written orientation k_xσ_x−k_yσ_y; the name does not establish permission in arbitrary C₂ᵥ settings. With this workshop’s xz/yz mirror axes, mirrors forbid that orientation. Changing crystal axes or the doublet representation requires transforming the whole model and symmetry operations consistently.

## Generators and covariance conditions

- **Rotation:**z angle2π/n, n=2,3,4; plane momenta/spin components rotate accordingly.
- **xz mirror:** momentum becomes (k_x,−k_y). Real spin is axial, so (σ_x,σ_y,σ_z) becomes (−σ_x,σ_y,−σ_z), not the polar-vector transformation.
- **Inversion:** in a same-parity doublet its matrix is ±I, leaving Pauli parts unchanged while k→−k.
- ** time reversal :**** T=iσ_yK, T²=−1, k/all spin components reverse.

The unitary condition is H(Rk)=UH(k)U† and the antiunitary condition H(−k)=U_TH(k)*U_T†. For a Hermitian Pauli expansion with real coefficients, time reversal equivalently reverses the Pauli vector. The program constrains every polynomial coefficient identically rather than comparing energies at a few sample momenta.

C₂ᵥ,C₃ᵥ,C₄ᵥ supply corresponding rotations and an xz mirror as reference generators. Disabling one leaves the group generated by survivors, not the original point group. Adding inversion can enlarge constraints.

## Linear algebra/projection meaning

The program assembles all linear constraints as Ac=0 and finds the nullspace by singular-value decomposition; singular values above 10⁻¹⁰ count as nonzero. With real orthonormal nullspace basis Q, inputs map to c_allowed=QQᵀc_input.

This is Euclidean orthogonal projection of the listed monomial coefficients. Renormalizing monomials changes the meaning of “nearest.” The result is a teaching representative in a declared metric, not a material fit, unique physical group-average prescription, or experimental correction. Constraints, nullity, and residuals explain which conditions exclude which combinations.

With rotation, mirror,  time reversal , C₂ᵥ allowed dimension 5, C₃ᵥ/C₄ᵥ3. C₄ᵥ permits constant/isotropic-quadratic scalars and Rashba linear terms; higher-order C₃ᵥ warping is outside second order.

## From coefficients to bands

The energies are E_±(k)=d₀(k)±|d(k)|. Plots compare input/constrained models along k_y=0; Γ splitting is 2|d(0)|.

 time reversal  requires d(−k)=−d(k), but generic k is not  time reversal  invariant; Rashba does not violate  time reversal . Same-parity inversion adds d(−k)=d(k); together d(k)=0. Broken inversion does not automatically break Γ Kramers.

Plots describe a local model only. Gaps, degeneracies and linear dispersion near Γ do not determine X-point behavior, full-lattice bands or Chern numbers; those need a periodic model and full-Brillouin-zone diagnostics. Orbital pseudospins, opposite-parity doublets, multiorbital bases and nontrivial space-group translation phases are also outside the current representation.

Method background: [Qsymm official documentation](https://qsymm.readthedocs.io/latest/). The workshop is an independent, scoped NumPy teaching implementation, not a complete Qsymm port or replacement for existing symbolic-Hamiltonian calculations.
